analysis.title: Collateralized Chip Obligations Go Into Reverse: Banks Head For The Exits As Credit Chiefs Warn Of A "Fear Factor"
key_insights: FT reports ING and Société Générale have put as much as $800 million of data center debt up for sale in recent weeks, including loans tied to Oracle's Stargate initiative with OpenAI.

ING's auction includes $500 million of loans linked to CyrusOne, EdgeConneX and Vantage plus Oracle-backed Project Jupiter in New Mexico. SocGen is shopping $300 million of project finance debt for Oracle's Project Lighthouse (Wisconsin) and Project Frontier (Texas). The three projects raised more than $56 billion in construction debt from dozens of banks last year.

Lighthouse and Frontier loans were quoted above 90 cents on the dollar. Jupiter, which is struggling to secure electricity, was expected to price in the mid-80s. Bids on ING's portfolio were due Nov 19.

The effort to offload data center debt has run for months as banks grow wary of concentrated exposure to AI and a handful of Big Tech and frontier lab names. It was stepped up to clean balance sheets by year-end after the midterms raised fears of a regulatory clampdown on US data centers.
Banks cannot hedge much of this exposure because confidentiality provisions in some data center loans bar lenders from CDS and synthetic risk transfers that require sharing loan information.

Banks are exploring credit insurance and risk-transfer deals and structuring deals in 144A format to reach a broader base of institutional buyers. Upcoming 144A deals: a $63 billion debt package for Anthropic and a $40 billion financing for SpaceX to buy AI chips. Some major lenders dropped out of the Anthropic deal over concentration concerns.
The Bank of England is asking UK banks for details of their data center loans. The ECB is working on a supervisory review of eurozone lenders' data center exposure.

At Bloomberg's Global Credit Forum, speakers described continued repricing in fixed income as rates stay elevated, spread widening in the weakest corporate debt, CoreWeave bonds at distressed levels, and French borrowing costs at the highest in more than two decades.

Bond traders are pricing at least a full 25bp Fed hike next month and nearly the same from the ECB. More than 90% of 100 respondents to Bloomberg's Markets Pulse survey expect the default rate for low-rated companies to end 2027 higher than this year. JPMorgan analysts say leveraged loan payment failures are set to more than double year-over-year.
CoreWeave junk bond yields rose above 15% last month and its CDS priced a more than 50% chance of default within five years. CoreWeave is now looking to raise money through investment grade debt.
Carlyle's Mark Jenkins said investors in AI data centers have no hurry given heavy supply coming, and that the technology risk of chip-backed asset-backed deals is difficult to underwrite.

Goldman's 2027 Global Credit Outlook expects modest spread widening: USD IG from 91bps to 105bps and USD HY from 337bps to 410bps by end of 2027. Its base case is a three-speed market: AI-related issuers with episodic widening, non-AI issuers range-bound, and leveraged finance's left tail under pressure (USD CCC average interest coverage below 1.0x).

Goldman estimates nearly $700 billion of AI-related gross issuance globally this year ($296 billion from the five hyperscalers, nearly $160 billion project finance). It forecasts $440 billion of direct hyperscaler issuance in 2027 (assuming 35% of capex is debt-funded) plus $545 billion of AI project finance ($225 billion data center shells, $320 billion chips and compute).

27 USD IG deals of $10 billion or more have priced this year totaling $500 billion, 66% AI-related. AI-related USD IG spreads are roughly 140bps vs about 100bps for non-AI, and AI HY is near 395bps vs roughly 265bps for non-AI BB/B (levels read off Goldman's chart by the author).

Goldman stays underweight Technology in IG and is moving underweight USD HY Technology. Its overweights are Banks, Health Care and Energy. It sees default rates rising to 4% in USD HY and 5% in USD leveraged loans by end-2027, with senior unsecured USD HY recoveries around $30 versus roughly $40 in 2021.

Goldman lists potential data center moratoria after the midterms among downside risks to its project finance forecast, and says 2027 AI risks (capacity constraints or insufficient monetization) are more likely to spill into broader macro weakness. It recommends using strength into year-end to reset macro hedges.

The ECB's Financial Stability Review says the shift toward debt finance invokes historical parallels with the dotcom and subprime bubbles and could spill over to euro area financial stability. It flags circular deals between cloud providers, AI labs and chipmakers and the opacity of AI-related debt.

market_movers.rationale: CoreWeave junk bond yields above 15% and CDS pricing a more than 50% five-year default chance. It is seeking investment grade debt. Bonds are at levels that typically signal distress.
Oracle-backed data center projects (Jupiter, Lighthouse, Frontier) are being sold by lenders. Jupiter is expected to price in the mid-80s after a force majeure notice over power permit delays.

The author argues Nvidia's backstops of AI financing are being withdrawn under Huang's successor, and that the Nvidia-linked $500 billion third-party compute capital platform has yet to produce a deal.

tension_points.bull_case: Lighthouse and Frontier loans quoted above 90 cents, described to the FT as routine portfolio management rather than acute stress. Goldman's base case is modest spread widening with most markets between the 30th and 50th percentile of post-GFC outcomes. CoreWeave says it has plenty of funding levers.
tension_points.bear_case: Jupiter expected in the mid-80s, banks selling with no hedge available, AI spreads about 40bps wider than non-AI in IG, a roughly $1 trillion supply wave in 2027, and the ECB's dotcom and subprime parallels.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Bids on ING's portfolio due Nov 19 clearing well below the mid-80s for Jupiter, or not clearing at all.

theme_stances.key_argument: Banks are selling data center debt and shifting risk to 144A buyers because they cannot hedge it.
theme_stances.evidence: the only hedge left is the exit

theme_stances.key_argument: Price has cleared the market so far, but there is a limit to how far investors will underwrite AI re-leveraging on pricing alone.
theme_stances.evidence: we think there is a limit to how far investors will underwrite this re-leveraging
